name: Infrastructure | Self-hosting
tagline: Self-hosted production environment — deployment, security, and day-to-day operations for internet-exposed services.
popTagline: Set up to gain hands-on experience with deployment, security basics, and everyday operational concerns in a self-hosted environment.
popOverview: The self-hosting of my personal websites and applications, from deployment to maintenance, operated end-to-end without managed platform guarantees. The result is a flexible setup that supports multiple applications and evolves with my needs.

sectionKeyPoints.Orchestration: Docker Swarm for container management, with secrets for sensitive data.

sectionKeyPoints.Routing: Traefik for dynamic HTTPS routing, with Nginx used inside images for static sites.

sectionKeyPoints.Security and monitoring: Root access disabled, UFW and fail2ban against brute force, and Grafana + Prometheus for insights into system performance.

sectionKeyPoints.Self-managed over managed platforms: Turnkey platforms limit flexibility and can hide costs; running my own setup forces explicit decisions.

sectionKeyPoints.Incremental, modular setup: Start simple, add components only when a real need appears, and refactor when complexity justifies it.

sectionKeyPoints.Automation where it pays off: Repetitive and error-prone steps are automated; automation that adds more abstraction than value is deferred.

sectionKeyPoints.Cost predictability vs scalability: Fixed, predictable costs, accepting manual scaling as a trade-off.

sectionKeyPoints.Debugging alone: Early issues led to better logging and observability, and simpler configurations that are easier to reason about.

sectionKeyPoints.Learning vs reliability: Stable, proven components stay untouched, kept apart from the experimental parts where learning is the goal.
